explanation: Owning a venture can mean unpredictable income, long workdays, and personal risk. Those demands are important to consider before starting.
hint: Imagine having no guaranteed paycheck, investing your own savings, and staying late whenever an urgent business problem appears.

subject: Entrepreneurship and Small Business Management
question: The ability to develop new ideas and to discover new ways of looking at problems and opportunities is called ________.
explanation: Creativity is the ability to see a problem or opportunity in a new way and imagine possible solutions.
hint: Imagine coming up with a clever way to reuse waste material; actually producing and selling it is a later step.

subject: Entrepreneurship and Small Business Management
question: An entrepreneurial “secret” for creating value in the marketplace is ________.

options.label: A
options.text: applying creativity and innovation to solve problems

explanation: Creativity finds a new approach; innovation turns that approach into a solution customers can use.
hint: New ideas matter when they are turned into real products, services, or improvements.

subject: Entrepreneurship and Small Business Management
question: Entrepreneurship is a constant process that relies on ________.

options.label: B
options.text: the ability to win over the consumer

options.label: C
options.text: creativity, innovation, and application in the marketplace

explanation: An idea creates value when it is developed into something useful and offered to customers. Creativity starts it; innovation puts it to work.
hint: New ideas matter when they are turned into real products, services, or improvements.

subject: Entrepreneurship and Small Business Management
question: ________ is necessary for building a competitive advantage and for business survival.
explanation: Creativity is the ability to see a problem or opportunity in a new way and imagine possible solutions.
hint: When every rival sells the same thing, the ability to imagine a useful fresh approach can keep a company from falling behind.

subject: Entrepreneurship and Small Business Management
question: Innovation is the ability to develop new ideas and to discover new ways of looking at problems and opportunities.
explanation: The statement is false because it reverses or overstates the business concept. Replace the claim with the standard definition.
hint: Having the idea for a better lunchbox is one stage; turning it into a working product is another. Which stage does the statement describe?

subject: Entrepreneurship and Small Business Management
question: An entrepreneur is a person who ________.

options.label: A
options.text: is willing to attempt to implement a business concept and then give up if it does not meet immediate expectations

options.label: B
options.text: understands the process of developing an idea and does not need to understand what it means to bring that idea to a viable business concept

options.label: C
options.text: knows that the concept they are about to develop will result in a profitable business

options.label: D
options.text: creates a new business concept for the purpose of achieving profit and growth by assembling the necessary resources to capitalize on identified opportunities

explanation: An entrepreneur brings an opportunity, resources, and willingness to take a risk together to launch a venture.
hint: Picture someone noticing an unmet customer need, gathering money and people, and accepting the risk of building a venture around it.

subject: Entrepreneurship and Small Business Management
question: Entrepreneurs who repeatedly start businesses and grow to a sustainable size before striking out again are known as ________ entrepreneurs.
explanation: A serial entrepreneur starts multiple businesses over time, often moving on after one venture becomes stable.
hint: Think of a television series: one episode follows another. This founder also moves on to another venture after building the previous one.

subject: Entrepreneurship and Small Business Management
question: An effective tool used to help assess ideas is the ________.
explanation: An idea dashboard helps compare several possible ventures using the same criteria, so the owner can see which idea is strongest.
hint: The tool's name borrows from the panel in a car that lets a driver scan several important signals in one place.

subject: Entrepreneurship and Small Business Management
question: The process of determining whether an entrepreneur’s idea is a viable foundation for creating a successful business is known as a(n) ________.
explanation: A feasibility analysis tests whether the idea has customers, workable operations, and enough resources to succeed before the owner commits heavily.
hint: Before committing, check whether the idea meets a customer need and can be carried out.

subject: Entrepreneurship and Small Business Management
question: A product or service feasibility analysis determines the degree to which a product or service idea appeals to potential customers and identifies the necessary resources.
explanation: A product or service feasibility check asks whether customers want the idea and what resources are needed to deliver it. Those answers help judge whether the idea is workable.
hint: Before making thousands of units, a founder checks whether customers want the product and whether the firm has what it needs to provide it.

subject: Entrepreneurship and Small Business Management
question: Entrepreneurs typically identify just one business idea for any given market need.
explanation: The statement is false because it reverses or overstates the business concept. Replace the claim with the standard definition.
hint: One problem can have several solutions: lunch delivery, meal subscriptions, and an office canteen could all meet the same need.

subject: Entrepreneurship and Small Business Management
question: The purpose of a feasibility study is to determine whether a business idea is worth pursuing.
explanation: A feasibility study checks demand, resources, and practical obstacles before the owner commits time and money. It helps decide whether the idea is worth pursuing.
hint: It is cheaper to investigate customers, resources, and costs before investing all your savings in an idea that may not work.

subject: Entrepreneurship and Small Business Management
question: Entrepreneurs who start businesses because they cannot find work any other way are called ________.
explanation: A necessity entrepreneur starts mainly because other employment is unavailable or does not meet their needs.
hint: Compare choosing a promising opening in the market with starting a firm because no other way to earn a living is available.

subject: Entrepreneurship and Small Business Management
question: Research and studies have isolated a set of characteristics that can predict who will succeed as an entrepreneur.
explanation: The statement is false because it reverses or overstates the business concept. Replace the claim with the standard definition.
hint: Two equally persistent and imaginative founders may have different outcomes because markets, timing, and resources also matter.

subject: Entrepreneurship and Small Business Management
question: Creativity is the ability to develop new ideas and to discover new ways of looking at problems and opportunities.
explanation: Creativity means imagining new ideas or new ways to view a problem. It helps entrepreneurs spot opportunities and possible solutions.
hint: Imagine seeing an ordinary discarded bottle and thinking of several useful things it could become; the ideas come before any product is built.

subject: Entrepreneurship and Small Business Management
question: When developing creative solutions to modern problems, entrepreneurs must ________.

options.label: A
options.text: go beyond merely using whatever has worked in the past

options.label: B
options.text: limit the creative process to only profitable ventures

options.label: C
options.text: remember what has worked in the past

explanation: Creative problem-solving tests new approaches when the old method does not fit the new problem.
hint: A new problem may need a fresh approach instead of repeating an old solution.

subject: Entrepreneurship and Small Business Management
question: All of the following represent barriers to creativity that entrepreneurs impose upon themselves except ________.

options.label: D
options.text: searching for more than one answer

explanation: Exploring several possible answers encourages creativity; stopping after the first idea can hide better solutions.
hint: Look for a behavior that opens up possibilities instead of stopping at the first idea.

subject: Entrepreneurship and Small Business Management
question: A(n) ________ is the process of examining a need in the market, developing a solution for that need, and determining the entrepreneur’s ability to successfully turn the idea into a business.
explanation: Idea assessment checks whether a customer need is real and whether the proposed solution and resources could meet it.
hint: Before committing, check whether the idea meets a customer need and can be carried out.

subject: Entrepreneurship and Small Business Management
question: All of the following are characteristics of the typical entrepreneur except ________.

options.label: A
options.text: confidence in his/her ability to succeed

explanation: Many entrepreneurs care about reaching a goal and building something of their own, not only earning money.
hint: Entrepreneurs are often driven more by reaching a goal than by money alone.

subject: Entrepreneurship and Small Business Management
question: List 5 benefits of entrepreneurship (5 marks) and discuss 1 of them in detail (10 marks).

answer.value: Independence and control over decisions; opportunity to pursue a passion; potential financial rewards; flexibility; personal achievement and community impact. Independence enables the owner to choose products, customers, and strategy.
accepted_values: Independence and control over decisions; opportunity to pursue a passion; potential financial rewards; flexibility; personal achievement and community impact. Independence enables the owner to choose products, customers, and strategy.

explanation: Owning a business can give people more control over their work and decisions than working under a supervisor.
hint: A founder can choose the work, put a passion into practice, and benefit if the idea succeeds. Think about what each freedom could mean in daily life.

subject: Entrepreneurship and Small Business Management
question: Differentiate creativity and innovations (10 marks) and give real-life examples of each (5 marks).

answer.value: Creativity is generating novel and useful ideas; innovation is implementing those ideas as marketable products, services, or processes. For example, conceiving a mobile-ordering concept is creativity; launching and refining an operational mobile-ordering app is innovation.
accepted_values: Creativity is generating novel and useful ideas; innovation is implementing those ideas as marketable products, services, or processes. For example, conceiving a mobile-ordering concept is creativity; launching and refining an operational mobile-ordering app is innovation.

explanation: Compare the choices by their defining feature: who owns them, who controls decisions, and who carries the risk. That makes the distinction clear.
hint: Imagining a new reusable cup is one step; developing it into a product customers can actually use and buy is another.

subject: Entrepreneurship and Small Business Management
question: List 5 of the 10 “mental blocks” that limit individual creativity (5 marks) and discuss how an entrepreneur can overcome any 1 of them (5 marks).

answer.value: Five mental blocks: focusing only on logic; rigidly following rules; seeking one right answer; being too practical; fearing mistakes. Overcome fear of mistakes by creating a safe setting for inexpensive experiments and learning from failures.
accepted_values: Five mental blocks: focusing only on logic; rigidly following rules; seeking one right answer; being too practical; fearing mistakes. Overcome fear of mistakes by creating a safe setting for inexpensive experiments and learning from failures.

explanation: An entrepreneur turns an opportunity into action by organizing resources and accepting uncertainty. A useful idea only creates value when it reaches customers.
hint: Imagine rejecting an idea because it breaks a rule, sounds impractical, or might fail. Those habits can stop a useful idea before it gets a chance.

subject: Entrepreneurship and Small Business Management
question: Discuss the components of Porter’s 5 forces competitive analysis (20 marks) and draw a figure to illustrate them (5 marks).

answer.value: Porter’s five forces: rivalry among existing competitors, threat of new entrants, threat of substitutes, bargaining power of buyers, and bargaining power of suppliers. Diagram: place industry rivalry at the center, with four surrounding arrows for entrants, substitutes, buyers and suppliers.
accepted_values: Porter’s five forces: rivalry among existing competitors, threat of new entrants, threat of substitutes, bargaining power of buyers, and bargaining power of suppliers. Diagram: place industry rivalry at the center, with four surrounding arrows for entrants, substitutes, buyers and suppliers.

explanation: Competition comes from five directions. Existing rivals compete for the same customers. New entrants may take a share of the market. Substitute products meet the same need another way. Buyers can press for lower prices, and suppliers can press for higher prices. Together, these pressures affect how much profit a business can keep.
hint: Picture a café squeezed by rival cafés, possible new cafés, home-brewed coffee, demanding customers, and powerful bean suppliers. Each source of pressure is a different force.
